title: signs, signals and road markings
objectives: Identify signs by their shape, colour and message, including regulatory, school, playground and crosswalk signs
Explain the rules set by lane use, turn control, parking and reserved lane signs
Identify warning, object marker, construction and information signs and the hazards they describe
State the meaning of railway signs, lane control signals and each traffic light indication
Explain the meaning of yellow lines, white lines and reserved lane road markings

sections.title: Regulatory, school, playground and crosswalk signs
points: Signs can be read three ways: by shape, colour, and the message printed on them.
Regulatory signs state driving laws — disregarding them is an offence under the B.C. Motor Vehicle Act.
A red octagon means stop completely and continue only when safe; a red-and-white triangle means yield the right-of-way.
A posted speed limit is the maximum legal speed when the road is bare and dry and visibility is good.
School zone signs are fluorescent yellow-green; reduce speed when children are present.
Slow traffic delaying five vehicles must use pullouts where regulatory pullout signs are posted.
At school and pedestrian crosswalks, yield to people crossing and follow any crossing guard's directions.
mustKnow: A school zone speed tab with only a speed limit is in effect from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on school days.
Playground zone — 30 km/h limit is in effect every day from dawn to dusk.
School zone signs are fluorescent yellow-green.
It is an offence under the B.C. Motor Vehicle Act to disregard regulatory signs.

check.q: A school zone sign has a tab underneath showing only a speed limit. When is that limit in effect?
choices: From 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on school days
Every day from dawn to dusk
Only when a crossing guard is present
check.explanation: A tab showing only the speed limit applies from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on school days.

check.q: When is the 30 km/h playground zone speed limit in effect?
choices: Every day from dawn to dusk
check.explanation: The playground zone 30 km/h limit is in effect every day from dawn to dusk.

sections.title: Lane use, turn control, parking and reserved lane signs
points: Lane use signs are mounted above or beside the lane before the intersection and show whether to turn or go straight.
In a designated lane you must follow the arrows, and you may not move into or out of it within an intersection.
Turn control signs are mounted directly above the intersection; you must follow the direction of the arrow.
Parking signs say where and when you may park; illegal parking can bring fines, towing, or both.
Some parking spots are reserved for vehicles displaying the disabled parking sign and carrying a person with disabilities.
Reserved lane signs are placed over or beside lanes reserved for buses or high occupancy vehicles (HOVs).
A white diamond painted on the road surface marks reserved lanes.
mustKnow: You may not move into or out of a designated lane while you are in an intersection.
A white diamond painted on the road surface marks reserved lanes.
HOV signs may show how many people must be in the vehicle to use the lane.

check.q: Where are turn control signs mounted?
choices: On the curb at the corner
On the far side of the crosswalk
check.explanation: Turn control signs are mounted directly above the intersection and you must follow the arrow.

check.q: What symbol painted on the road surface marks a reserved lane?
check.explanation: Reserved lanes for buses and HOVs are marked with a white diamond painted on the road surface.

sections.title: Warning, object marker, construction and information signs
points: Most warning signs are yellow and diamond-shaped, warning of possible hazards ahead such as curves, merges or steep hills.
Examples: winding road, hidden side road, road narrows, two-way traffic, slippery road, and stop sign ahead.
A school crosswalk ahead warning sign is fluorescent yellow-green.
Object markers are mounted directly on obstructions and tell you to keep right or left.
Construction signs warn of work zones: obey traffic-control persons, posted speeds, stay back from equipment, pass only when safe.
A recommended exit speed sign means drive slower in poor conditions.
Information and destination signs give destinations, route numbers and facilities; distances are in kilometres.
mustKnow: Most warning signs are yellow and diamond-shaped.
Object markers are mounted on obstructions.
Destination sign distances are in kilometres.

check.q: What shape and colour are most warning signs?
check.explanation: Most warning signs are yellow and diamond-shaped and warn of possible hazards ahead.
Object markers are mounted on obstructions and direct you to keep right or left.

sections.title: Railway signs, lane control signals and traffic lights
points: Railway crossings are marked with signs or pavement markings and may have mechanical or electrical warning devices.
You must always yield to trains; at a gated crossing, stay stopped until the gate is fully raised.
Lane control signals over a lane: a green arrow means drive in this lane; a red signal means do not.
If lane control signals over all lanes flash yellow, slow down and proceed with caution.
Steady red: stop; after a full stop you may turn right, or left onto a one-way street, unless a sign forbids it.
Flashing green is a pedestrian-controlled light; flashing red means stop, then continue only when safe.
A flashing green arrow with a steady red light allows a left turn while through traffic must stop.
A steady white rectangular transit priority signal means only buses may go.
mustKnow: You must always yield to trains.
Steady yellow — slow down and stop before the intersection unless you can't safely stop in time.
Flashing green — pedestrian-controlled light — go only if the intersection is clear.
Transit priority signal — steady white rectangular light — only buses may go on this signal.

check.q: You approach an intersection showing a flashing green arrow with a steady red light. What may you do?
choices: Turn left; through traffic must stop
check.explanation: A flashing green arrow with a steady red light allows a left turn while through traffic stops for the red.

check.q: What does a flashing green traffic light mean?
choices: An advance turn signal is coming
It is a pedestrian-controlled light — go only if the intersection is clear
Speed up before the light changes
check.explanation: A flashing green light is pedestrian-controlled; go only if the intersection is clear.

sections.title: Road markings — yellow lines, white lines and reserved lanes
points: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions; white lines separate traffic moving in the same direction.
Broken yellow line: passing allowed when safe; single yellow line: passing allowed with extra caution.
Broken plus solid yellow: pass only when safe and the broken line is on your side; double solid: no passing.
A double broken yellow line marks a reversible lane — lane control signals show whether you may use it.
A two-way left-turn lane is shared by drivers travelling in opposite directions for left turns.
Solid white line: do not change lanes; broken white line: lane changing allowed when safe.
Bicycle lanes are marked with a bicycle outline; keep right of painted islands and never drive on or over them.
It is illegal to drive over freshly painted, wet pavement markings.
mustKnow: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions.
White lines are used to separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
Double solid line — no passing allowed.
HOV lanes are marked with thick solid or broken lines and white diamond symbols.

check.q: What do yellow lines on the road indicate?
choices: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction
The edge of the right shoulder
Traffic moving in opposite directions on either side
check.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions — traffic comes toward you across a yellow line.

check.q: You are driving beside a broken yellow line with a solid yellow line beyond it. When may you pass?
choices: Only when safe and the broken line is on your side
check.explanation: With a broken and solid line, you may pass only when it is safe and the broken line is on your side.

summary: Read signs by shape, colour and message: red octagon stops you, red-and-white triangle yields, yellow diamond warns.
School zone tab limits run 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on school days; playground 30 km/h runs every day, dawn to dusk.
Follow lane use and turn control arrows, and never change into or out of a designated lane inside an intersection.
Always yield to trains, and know every traffic light meaning, including flashing green (pedestrian-controlled) and white transit signals.
Yellow lines separate opposing traffic and white lines separate same-direction traffic; pass only where markings allow.
